comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: Retains refuge in God, joyful celebration, and divine protection. It moves welcome and refuge ahead of rejoicing, changes the beneficiaries from 'all' who seek refuge to 'us,' and omits the closing identification of those who love God's name and exult in him.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: Adds an open-armed welcome and running for cover. Rejoicing becomes a party, its perpetual duration becomes 'all night,' and covering people becomes guarding their celebration. Repeated fragments provide lyrical emphasis.

comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: The English retains refuge in God, communal joy, and divine protection. It changes 'all who take refuge' into 'we/us,' reduces everlasting rejoicing to an all-night celebration, and leaves out the closing identification of those who love God's name and exult in him.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: An open-armed welcome adds hospitality imagery. 'Party' recasts rejoicing in colloquial terms, while 'Stand guard over our celebration' makes the celebration, rather than the people, the object of protection.
